A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Free Space Prior research. All 12 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v3, including their supplementary sections, are readable. Equations, experiments, figures and tables can be reliably matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original cleanup-quality and runtime experiments on Nerfbusters, density analyses, a ray-sampling ablation and qualitative evaluations on additional datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds geometric evaluations, sampling and view-density studies, additional architecture and task demonstrations, and a noisy-input experiment.

M1.justification: The main post-hoc procedure, global sampling and combined reconstruction/free-space loss remain unchanged. However, v3 Section 5.2 and Table 4 add an application of the loss during NeRF training from scratch, eliminating the separate cleanup stage. This is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: v3 Figure 1 and Section 5.4 add LeRF language-based scene understanding, Seathru underwater scenes and KITTI-360 semantic segmentation. Appendix A.8 also evaluates Gaussian-corrupted input images. The original Nerfbusters coverage and supplementary Garden, Basket, Playground and Trevi examples are retained.

E2.justification: The central Nerfbusters comparison retains Nerfacto, Nerfbusters, BayesRays and Gaussian Splatting, while adding an L2 weight-regularization baseline and a training-time FSP variant in Figures 3 and 11 and Table 4. These are limited additions to the existing comparison set.

E3.justification: v3 adds geometric protocols using 35,000-point clouds and depth references from a NeRF trained on training and test images, sparse/dense training-view configurations, additional NeRF backbones, and varying cleanup sample counts. Appendix A.4 additionally evaluates GT-mask PSNR. The original predicted-mask benchmark and its stated pretraining and cleanup budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test geometry preservation, cleanup sample-count sensitivity, sparse/dense-view robustness, training-time FSP, noisy-input failure and underwater density behavior. The original ray-only sampling ablation and terrestrial density analyses remain. Appendix A.5 interprets the existing lambda sweep rather than introducing a new sweep.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Reporting point estimates and averages across benchmark scenes remains the practice in v3.

E6.justification: All shared benchmark rows in v1 Table 1 and v3 Table 4 are identical, as are the reported cleanup runtimes and ray-sampling ablation scores. v3 adds L2 results, including PSNR 17.10 and coverage 87.09%, six training-time FSP rows, geometric and sparse/dense results in Tables 2–3, GT-mask results, and new qualitative and robustness outcomes.

T1.justification: The rendering, reconstruction and free-space loss equations remain mathematically equivalent despite renumbering and notation cleanup. v3's L2/ridge analogy and underwater discussion add conceptual explanations, without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of efficient artifact removal, optimization of unseen regions and no additional inference memory remain. v3 adds explicit generalization across NeRF architectures and datasets as a headline contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion, extending v1's emphasis on efficient cleanup.

C2.justification: v3 explains density-output versus weight regularization, interprets lambda robustness, and qualifies the free-space assumption for underwater imaging. Its new limitations section specifies failures involving inconsistent images, moving objects, poor bundle adjustment and input noise; Appendix A.8 demonstrates persistent color bias. These substantially expand v1's more general discussion of static-scene epistemic uncertainty.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies the predicted-mask accumulation threshold of 0.98, visualization lambda settings and reconstruction sampling of 4,096 rays with 352 samples each. It retains the main hardware and training-budget disclosures, but omits v1's explicit 32/512 samples-per-ray ablation settings and 2^18-point histogram sampling count.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Zip-NeRF, OpenNeRF, LeRF, Seathru-NeRF and KITTI-360. Related work expands the discussion of distortion/interlevel regularization and its remaining floater problem. The principal positioning against Nerfbusters, BayesRays and existing priors is retained.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites and condenses the introduction, background and results narrative, separates density analysis from ablations, and reorganizes the experimental sections. Implementation details move to the appendix, supplementary material moves after the references, and dedicated robustness and limitations sections are introduced.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a predominantly single-column layout. v3 replaces the point-cloud teaser with a multi-architecture comparison, redraws the method diagram, rearranges density plots, converts the runtime graph into a table, expands qualitative grids and the results table, and adds several experimental displays.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for scene preservation and practical applicability through geometric consistency tests, sparse/dense-view evaluations, an L2 comparison and broader architecture demonstrations. The explicit limitations and noisy-input failure example also better qualify the cleanup claims. Cross-architecture evidence remains largely qualitative, and some original ablation details are lost, but the added validation addresses important gaps in v1 while preserving its original benchmark evidence.
